articles.title: Galaxy Swirl
articles.summary: Near-uniform M and R with faint repeated Cc dots; no spiral arms or star points resolved at this size. Reads as a soft wavy ripple or fine scroll sheen on metal; on satin it is almost plain.
articles.what: Creates spiral galaxy arm metallic patterns with scattered star cluster highlight points throughout Up close: A repeating tile of tiny comma-shaped spiral curls about 30 px wide, like little paisley or wave swirls, packed in rows. They show clearly as bright and dark curls on the metallic half and only as faint dashes on satin. No obvious star cluster points at this scale. From a distance: Reads as a soft wavy ripple or fine scroll sheen on metal; on satin it is almost plain. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Sparkle & Micro-Metal (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: roof, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Sparkle & Micro-Metal", or search for "Galaxy Swirl".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and deck lid: open panels show the curls
Best on metallic bases
Numbers keep their colour; the swirl is faint and does not hurt legibility.
Almost invisible: faint dashes in the highlight
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, satin.
pitfalls: Not a galaxy colour graphic: despite the name it adds no colour or red, only shine variation
Not guilloche engine turning: curls are individual comma shapes, not continuous lines
Avoid: do not promise spiral arms or star clusters, verify at larger size before cosmic use.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

articles.title: Anisotropic Radial
articles.summary: Sharp angular metallic bands radiate from a center point, like a starburst of brushed shine. Reads as a smooth, slightly silky sheen; across a whole wheel-sized disc it would become a spun-metal star, but panel-sized it is nearly plain.
articles.what: Radial anisotropic star pattern — sin(atan2 × N/2)^p formula creates sharp angular metallic bands from disc center, FBM run-out perturbation, distinct from brushed_radial Up close: In this 512 px crop it is almost smooth: a few scattered pin-prick sparkles and a couple of thin horizontal scratch lines, with no visible star. The radial star bands only develop across a larger disc, so here you mostly see a clean gradient sheen. From a distance: Reads as a smooth, slightly silky sheen; across a whole wheel-sized disc it would become a spun-metal star, but panel-sized it is nearly plain. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Directional Metal & Brush (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Highlight looks slightly watery rather than textured. From a distance: Reads as a smooth, slightly uneven sheen with no visible pattern; you just see the highlight look a touch liquid.
